concepts.title: Line Symmetry and Lines of Symmetry
concepts.definition: A figure has line symmetry when it can be folded along a line so that the two halves match exactly; the fold is a line of symmetry, and figures may have one, many or no such lines.
concepts.key_idea: A line of symmetry is a mirror inside the figure: each half is the exact reflection of the other.

concepts.title: Rotational Symmetry
concepts.definition: A figure has rotational symmetry when a half-turn or other turn about its centre brings it to look exactly like itself; the number of times it matches in one full rotation is its order of rotational symmetry.
concepts.key_idea: Spin the figure and count the matches: the number of self-matches in one turn is its rotational order.

concepts.title: Symmetric Figures in Nature and Art
concepts.definition: Symmetry decorates the world: butterfly wings, flowers, rangoli patterns and architecture show lines of symmetry, and artists and nature alike repeat mirrored halves for balance and beauty.
concepts.key_idea: Symmetry is design language: nature and art both speak it with mirrored halves and turns.

concepts.title: Completing Symmetric Figures
concepts.definition: Given half a figure and its line of symmetry, the whole can be completed by reflecting each point: every dot on one side finds its partner at the same distance on the other side of the mirror line.
concepts.key_idea: Mirror lines double everything faithfully: equal distances on both sides rebuild the hidden half.
